catalog_features.default: every catalog flag is OFF by default (each is strict "true", read once per process); with a flag off the server behaves as if the feature did not exist

features.affects: POST /api/execute `version` (a positive integer or "latest") and `digest` (sha256:, wins over version) are honoured, and `path` may be a reference form. A `kind: playbook` step sends `version` as an integer only, so it asks for @latest or a digest through its `path`. A child of a pinned execution with no version resolves to the root's pinned version. With the flag off, version/digest are ignored and the path resolves to its latest version
features.name: execution_pinning

features.affects: `@latest` (e.g. a `kind: playbook` path `a/b@latest`) inside a pinned tree, only for paths the root lists in metadata.catalog.hot_reload; otherwise refused, never silently downgraded
features.name: hot_reload
discovery
features.serves: POST /api/catalog/peer/resolve (signed, trusted peers only), POST /api/catalog/locate (internal token); imports under peer/<instance>/<path>

features.affects: locate fetches a reference's own source URI; fail closed, nothing is fetched without an allowlist
features.name: uri_fetch

reference_forms: <path>                 the pinned version inside a pinned tree, else latest
<path>@latest          latest; inside a pinned tree only with hot reload allowed
<path>@sha256:<64hex>  this name, and it must have this body
sha256:<64hex>         this body, under any name
catalog_features.reference_forms_accepted_by: POST /api/catalog/resolve and /api/catalog/sources (CAS), catalog locate (discovery), and, with pinning on, the `path` of POST /api/execute and of a `kind: playbook` step. A reference in `path` plus a `version`/`digest` field is refused, not merged.

source_scheme_forms.reads: one row from an operator-owned Postgres table with columns path (text), version (integer), content (text); without version the highest version for the path
source_scheme_forms.rules: the alias names a credential in this server's credential store (host/port/user/password/database, or connection_string), never user:pass in the URI; schema and table are identifiers [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* of at most 63 bytes; path is required; version is a positive integer

source_scheme_forms.cluster_note: the catalog tier holds records only when the server records registrations (NOETL_CATALOG_LOG=shadow) and the worker relay takes the server as the tier's producer (NOETL_EHDB_CATALOG_MIRROR_SOURCE=server, unset by default); otherwise the read finds nothing or the relay reports the tier disabled
source_scheme_forms.reads: a registration record in the cluster's EHDB catalog tier, via the worker relay; the record's content_sha256 is checked before the body is returned; found by a paged scan of the tier (a keyed lookup is TARGET)

executable_note: Kinds the parser accepts. Which kinds a live worker can execute is reported by workers (RFC dsl-knowledge-base Phase 3) and is not known to this process.

keys.input_schema: required; written by hand, never derived from workload; also the tools/call argument allowlist
keys.result_step: optional; the step whose result is returned

metadata_extensions.serves: POST /api/mcp (one MCP tool per exposed playbook)

keys.card: required mapping; card.name and card.description required, card.version and card.skills optional
keys.input_schema: required unless expose.mcp.input_schema is set; written by hand; the argument allowlist

keys.(list): globs over sub-playbook paths, read from the ROOT playbook only; at most 64, each 1-512 chars; malformed entries are ignored, so a typo only narrows the policy

metadata_extensions.serves: an explicit `@latest` sub-playbook reference inside this root's pinned execution tree

tool_kinds.availability: Needs the server gate AND a worker started with NOETL_WORKER_AGENT_TOOL=true (noetl/worker#398, noetl-tools 4.5.0); otherwise the worker fails the command as an unknown tool. The shared pool refuses `framework: claude-code`. A playbook-bound `tools:` entry (`playbook: <path>`) is refused before the first model call unless the worker also sets NOETL_WORKER_AGENT_PLAYBOOK_TOOLS=true (noetl/worker v6.14.0); see the manifest's worker_runtime.agent.
tool_kinds.name: agent

tool_kinds.availability: Runs on any noetl/worker: noetl-tools McpTool, wrapped by the worker's WorkerMcpTool for auth headers. Only the server gate is needed.
tool_kinds.name: mcp

tool_kinds.availability: Runs on any noetl/worker (noetl-tools PlaybookTool). Fields: `path` or `catalog_id`, `version` (integer), `payload`/`args`, `return_step`, `return_result`. With NOETL_CATALOG_PINNING on, `path` may be a catalog reference (`a/b@3`, `a/b@latest`, `a/b@sha256:...`, `sha256:...`, a source URI) and the child resolves inside the root's pin; see the manifest's catalog_features.
tool_kinds.name: playbook

tool_kinds.availability: Runs on a noetl/worker built with its `wasm-plugin` cargo feature (on by default and in the shipped image), which routes it to the plug-in host instead of the tool registry. Step: `plugin: { path: <string>, version: <integer>, entry: <export, default run> }` plus optional `input` (sent to the plug-in as `args`). The module is loaded from the catalog. Since noetl/worker v6.13.0 every call runs under fuel, wall-clock and memory limits that are ON by default; see the manifest's worker_runtime.wasm_limits.
tool_kinds.name: wasm

agent.budget_note: positive integers; anything else keeps the default; the model cannot override them (max_turns is the session's own)
agent.event_note: emitted on the agent's own execution by the hosted loop only (NOETL_WORKER_AGENT_PLAYBOOK_TOOLS=true), through the normal emit path

event_types.context: turn, tool_use_id, tool, binding, playbook, child_execution_id, is_error, duration_ms, input and result previews (2 KiB)
turns, tool_calls, child_execution_ids, duration_ms; or refused: tool_call_budget

playbook_tools.behaviour: the worker hosts the agent loop; each playbook-bound call starts a child execution (kind: playbook, return_result: true, parent = this execution) that runs on whatever pool its playbook targets; its result is the next turn's tool_result; a failed child is an is_error tool result
playbook_tools.default: OFF (strict "true"); without it a playbook-bound tools: entry is refused before the first model call
playbook_tools.not_durable: the loop lives in one command on one worker: if that worker dies mid-loop the step retries from the first turn and children that already ran run again (orchestrator-driven resume is TARGET)

tool_entry_forms.other: `mcp_servers:` / `agents:` entries are answered inside the agent session, as before
tool_entry_forms.playbook_bound: { name, description, input_schema, playbook: <catalog path>, result_step: <step> (optional; without it the child's last step result) }

worker_runtime.note: Read by noetl/worker, not by this server; the values here are the worker's code defaults. Which worker version a cluster runs is the cluster's fact, not this file's.

wasm_limits.default: ON: every limit applies by default; set a variable to 0 / off / none / unlimited to remove that one limit; an unparseable value keeps the default
wasm_limits.on_exceed: the module is stopped and the step fails with an error naming the variable
